inj.note: After dropping their sixth straight game Sunday, the Eagles now sit at 2-6 on the season and could be motivated to explore moving veteran players for draft capital ahead of the deadline. Barkley -- who is under contract through 2028 -- apparently won't be among the pieces the Eagles consider moving, as the team is counting on re-emerging as a playoff contender next season rather than embracing a long-term rebuilding effort. Though he'll be suiting up for a Week 9 matchup with the division-leading Giants, Barkley could continue to have his playing time managed while he gets ramped back up from hamstring and back injuries. He played just 22 of the Eagles' 68 offensive snaps in the loss to Washington, finishing with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown and a 24-yard reception on his lone target.

news.h: Saquon Barkley staying put in Philly
news.d: Tim McManus breaks down Philadelphia's decision to not trade Saquon Barkley.

news.h: Saquon Barkley has assurances he won't be traded, wants to help Eagles 'fix it'
news.d: Speaking after Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley told reporters he has received assurances from the front office that he will remain with the club beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

news.h: Sources: Saquon Barkley won't be traded by deadline despite Eagles' struggles
news.d: Saquon Barkley will not be traded before the trade deadline, putting an end to speculation that the Eagles RB could be on the move.

news.h: Eagles' Saquon Barkley carries no injury designation for Commanders matchup
news.d: Saquon Barkley, who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and was a limited participant Friday, carries no designation into Sunday's game.

news.h: Eagles star Saquon Barkley says he was forced to divest Exchange B equity stake
news.d: Eagles star Saquon Barkley said he was forced to divest his equity stake in Exchange B to comply with NFL rules.
